newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Nanshan Development loan raised to US$35 mln.
newsitem.headline: China Nanshan Development loan raised to US$35 mln.

text.p: The transferable term loan facility for China Nanshan Development (Group) Inc, Shenzhen Chiwan Wharf Holdings and Shenzhen Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base Co has been raised to $35 million from $25 million due to oversubscription, arranger NatWest Markets said.
The borrowers are all Sino-foreign joint ventures based in Shenzhen, China. Chiwan Wharf and Chiwan Petroleum are subsidiaries of China Nanshan.
Proceeds of the loan will be used to partially finance the construction of berths and grain silos located at terminal six of the Chiwan harbour.
The facility has a maturity of five years with a lenders' put option at the end of year three. It pays a margin of 120 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 143 basis points.
Arranger NatWest Markets committed to US$7.5 million.
Lead managers are Credit Suisse, with US$7.5 million, and China Construction Bank Hong Kong branch, ING Bank Shenzhen branch and Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, with US$5 million each.
Managers are Development Bank of Singapore, with US$3 million, and Banca di Roma Shanghai branch, with US$2 million.
